EQUITY: GLOBAL AUTOS & AUTO PARTS
Global outlook cut as China demand underwhelms
Rising China-made exports could reignite trade tensions across key auto markets
April sales were up 2% y-y, led by the strength in India

Global auto sales volume, based on the sales trends across the 18 countries we track, rose 2% y-y in April. Excluding China and Russia, sales in the rest of the world rose 5% y-y, led by India, where volumes increased 25% y-y, excluding commercial vehicles. This was partly offset by a 6% y-y decline in the US, where comparisons were tougher due to pull-forward demand in 2025, as consumers rushed to secure pre-tariff inventory at dealerships.

In China, wholesale auto sales declined for the fifth consecutive month. Weak domestic demand, following the expiry of tax exemptions and reduced trade-in subsidies, continued to outweigh strong export growth.
We have revised our global forecasts compared to six months ago
We now expect global auto sales to decline 1% y-y in 2026 and grow 2% in 2027 (Fig. 3), compared with our forecast six months ago, when we expected a 2% y-y growth in both the years.

The largest change is in China. We have revised down our estimates for new vehicle sales in China by 2.23mn units in 2026 and by 2.04mn units in 2027. These figures refer to cumulative domestic passenger vehicle registrations and commercial vehicle wholesales, as noted in Fig. 3.
This downward revision is partly offset by stronger expectations for India. We have revised up our annual sales outlook for India by 0.47mn units in 2026 and by 0.49mn units in 2027.
China's push to grow auto exports could lead to renewed trade tensions

We have revised down our China sales forecasts because domestic demand has underwhelmed following the expiry of tax exemptions for new energy vehicles and stricter requirements for trade-in subsidies.

Given the patchiness of China auto data, no single measure gives a complete picture. However, the underlying trend in domestic passenger vehicle demand looks weak. Based on passenger vehicle registrations, Jan-Apr 2026 SAAR was at 17.33mn units, well below the Jan-Apr 2025 SAAR of 21.10mn units and the full-year 2025 SAAR of 23.59mn units.

There could still be a sequential recovery in 2H26, particularly if consumers respond to new models with updated technology and/or additional national consumption subsidies. However, weak domestic demand makes it difficult to rebalance China auto sales toward the local consumer.

Against that backdrop, our China Autos colleagues have raised their China auto export sales forecasts to 7.37mn units for 2026, up 19% versus their prior estimate, and to 8.10mn units for 2027, up 24% versus their prior estimate. They expect domestic Chinese EV OEMs to gain further momentum in global markets.

We agree that, in the absence of a stronger domestic recovery, OEMs are likely to focus more heavily on exports. This applies to both domestic Chinese OEMs and transplants. Export growth helps keep production running, supports employment, and sustains revenue flows to local governments. But the scale of China's export push also raises the risk that trade tensions resurface.

Using a simple extrapolation, if China-made auto exports continue to ramp up in 2026 and 2027, we estimate that China-made vehicles' share of auto sales in these markets would rise from \(15\%\) in 2025 to \(18\%\) in 2026 and \(22\%\) in 2027.

Barring Australia, which no longer has a domestic mass-market auto manufacturing industry, we think it would be difficult for the remaining markets to absorb such a sharp increase in China-made auto imports without putting pressure on domestic auto employment. For that reason, we do not think the recent trade tensions are behind us. Rather, we think they are likely to become a recurring feature of the global auto market if China's domestic demand remains weak and export growth continues to accelerate.

When JGBs for individual investors are sold before maturity, an amount calculated via the following formula will be subtracted from the par value of the bond plus accrued interest: (1) for 10-year variable rate bonds, an amount equal to the two preceding coupon payments (before tax) x 0.79685 will be used, (2) for 5-year and 3-year fixed rate bonds, an amount equal to the two preceding coupon payments (before tax) x 0.79685 will be used. When inflation-indexed JGBs are purchased via public offerings, secondary distributions (uridashi deals), or other OTC transactions with NOM Securities, only the purchase price shall be paid, with no sales commission charged. Inflation-indexed JGBs carry the risk of losses, as prices fluctuate in line with changes in market interest rates and fluctuations in the nationwide consumer price index. The notional principal of inflation-indexed JGBs changes in line with the rate of change in nationwide CPI inflation from the time of its issuance. The amount of the coupon payment is calculated by multiplying the coupon rate by the notional principal at the time of payment. The maturity value is the amount of the notional principal when the issue becomes due. For JI17 and subsequent issues, the maturity value shall not undercut the face amount.
